Subject: Vectorization operational profile & next steps

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick write-up of what we heard and a proposed plan so we have alignment. Please flag anything we missed.

Summary of current state (from our call)
- Product: e‑commerce search + personalized recommendations for NimbleCommerce marketplaces.
- Current stack: PostgreSQL for catalog, Milvus for vectors (self-hosted on EC2), lightweight API layer on Node.js + Lambdas for spikes.
- Index size & growth: ~120M vectors today, expected 20–30% growth next 12 months.
- Query profile: avg QPS 80–130 depending on sale events, peak ~450 QPS on major campaigns.
- Ingestion patterns: nightly bulk reindex (full snapshot) + streaming incremental updates from order stream (~1k vectors/day).

Pain points you called out
- P95 search latency is inconsistent; spikes during campaigns causing timeouts in frontend (JavaScript client).
- Running separate reranker (BERT-based) adds 80–200ms to end-to-end time and is billed as a separate service.
- Cost: vector infra and rerank together are the single largest variable operational cost.
- Operational complexity: Milvus tuning and periodic reindex failures during large imports.

Success criteria (mutually agreed)
- Latency: end-to-end search + rerank P95 <= 150ms for typical traffic; 250ms acceptable at peak campaign load with graceful degradation.
- Relevance: recall@10 >= 0.85 on your internal benchmark set; top-3 relevance uplift >= 12% vs current.
- Cost: target <= $400 per 1M queries (search + rerank) over a monthly average.
- Reliability: automated fallback to a cheaper model/replica within <30s when primary cluster is degraded.

Operational profile we recommend exploring (outline)
- Serving: Redwood dedicated pool with autoscaling preserving a hot KV cache for sharded Milvus-style indices.
- Rerank: colocated CPU/GPU rerank nodes to avoid cross-service network tail latency; optional quantized reranker for lower-cost paths.
- Batching: continuous micro-batching for low-latency paths (20–40ms batching window) + larger bulk batches for reindex jobs to optimize throughput.
- Caching: prefix and query-result TTLs tuned around campaign patterns; ephemeral per-session caches for personalization.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Share a sample of your benign dataset (1–2k vectors and the matching ground truth file) — link or Drive upload.
2) Security: please confirm whether you need SOC2 evidence and if an NDA/DPA is required prior to sending logs.
3) Tech deep-dive: propose a 60-minute session with your infra lead, Aditya, and Karthik next week to go through ingestion, indexing, and rerank placement. Proposed slots: Tue 12/8 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 12/9 14:00–15:00 PT.
4) Trial: we can spin up a short PoC (2–3 weeks) with a small dedicated pool and a shared benchmark harness.

Attachments: Nimble_PoC_spec.pdf (PoC scope), redwood-pricing-quote.xlsx (estimate)

Thanks — I’ll follow up internally to schedule the deep-dive once you confirm preferred slot.

Best,

Thanks Stephanie — this is helpful and captures the call well. A couple clarifications and one ask: 

Clarifications
- Our reranker today runs on a small GPU fleet (g4dn) and is invoked for the top 50 candidates; average per-call latency is ~120ms but we see tails to 350ms on heavy nights.
- Milvus is currently sharded by category; cross-category queries hit multiple shards and are the common source of variance.

Ask
- Before we share the dataset, can you confirm what minimal access you need? Specifically: sample vectors + query log (anonymized) and a small set of labeled queries for relevance evaluation. We need to check with procurement.

We can do Tue 12/8 10:00 PT — that works for the infra team. I’ll invite our infra lead (I’ll add them to the invite after I check calendar).

Also — can you include an estimated snapshot of expected monthly spend for the PoC (rough ballpark) so procurement has a number to assess?
